phrases.text: New Year's Day. Plant a little hope. A small pot will do.
January 1. The year grew a number. I will catch up slowly.
Valentine's Day. No roses. Just grass with good intentions.
February 14. A little care for yourself counts as tending.
April Fools. I am a large tree. Still downloading the height.
April 1. I planted a joke. The punchline has not sprouted.
June 1. Keep a little curiosity. It uses very little soil.
June 1. A little play need not grow into a useful result.
Christmas Eve. Wishing your thoughts a gentler breeze.
December 24. Peace is a good word. Needs no pruning.
Christmas. Trees handle the lights. I provide a little green.
December 25. A leaf-sized good wish. No actual leaves picked.
Last day of the year. Not all the roots are visible.
December 31. No need to uproot yourself to prove you grew.
February 29. The calendar grew an extra leaf.
Leap day. An extra day may be an ordinary one. That is fine.
The first again. Fresh calendar soil. Same slow roots.
New month. Give the small plans a little room to breathe.
Happy Lunar New Year. A small greeting from a small plant.
Lunar New Year. Steadier roots. A little more ease above them.
Lantern Festival riddle: green, slow to answer. It is me.
Lantern Festival. Good wishes in a little round bundle. Like me.
Mid-Autumn. Round moon, round clump. Some visual agreement.
Mid-Autumn Festival. Wishing you a small patch of comfort.
